evals.prompt: Add an authenticated JSON route to a standalone Cloud inventory application and expose its typed browser client.
evals.expected_output: Uses current Cloud documentation, identifies the application as owner, separates route policy from resource authorization, validates input, exports the Hono router type, and verifies the HTTP seam.
expectations: The response reads the current Cloud contract through the documentation MCP or explicitly states reduced documentation mode.
The implementation separates route-entry policy from resource authorization.
The final Hono router type is the browser client's contract.
Verification exercises the HTTP boundary.

evals.prompt: The local gateway returns 502 for /app/inventory even though the inventory container is running. Diagnose and fix it.
evals.expected_output: Builds a red-capable route check, verifies app.start registration and declared prefixes before changing code, keeps the fix scoped, and reruns the original gateway request.
expectations: The diagnosis does not treat a running process as proof of route readiness.
It checks declared prefixes, mounted Hono routes, app.start, and gateway registration.
The final check repeats the original gateway request.

evals.prompt: Add a reusable async combobox to Cloud and use it in Contacts.
evals.expected_output: Searches the UI collection, assigns portable behavior to packages/ui and domain composition to Contacts, covers SSR and hydration behavior, updates Markdown context and a representative live state, and verifies public imports.
expectations: The response searches the UI documentation before creating a primitive.
Portable behavior belongs to shared UI while Contacts owns domain composition.
The change covers accessibility, SSR, hydration, Markdown context, and a representative live state.

evals.prompt: After an invoice is committed, send a retry-safe notification and start a durable follow-up workflow.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the invoice transaction authoritative, performs effects after commit, uses stable event or effect keys, derives recipients from trusted state, and verifies notification and workflow recovery seams.
expectations: The domain transaction commits before external effects run.
Retries reuse stable event or effect keys.
Recipients and authorization come from trusted server state.
Verification covers notification delivery and workflow recovery.

evals.prompt: Rename a private helper inside the Mail application without changing its behavior.
evals.expected_output: Keeps ownership in Mail, performs a focused refactor, verifies existing behavior, and explicitly avoids unnecessary public documentation changes.
expectations: The work remains owned by Mail and avoids unrelated cleanup.
Existing behavior receives focused verification.
The response does not create public documentation for an unchanged internal contract.

evals.prompt: Add an authenticated route to a standalone Cloud app, but the Cloud documentation MCP is missing from the agent session.
evals.expected_output: Stops before implementation, asks the application author to configure cloud-dev-mcp with https://cloud.k2b.dev/_fibel/mcp and restart the agent session, and enters reduced mode only when the author cannot connect it.
expectations: The agent asks the application author to configure the Cloud documentation MCP instead of silently implementing from memory.
The response names cloud-dev-mcp, https://cloud.k2b.dev/_fibel/mcp, and an agent-session restart.
Reduced documentation mode is explicit and used only when the application author cannot connect the MCP.
No product change is proposed before the documentation path is resolved.

evals.prompt: Change the title of an existing dashboard in my running Cloud installation.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as operating an existing installation and routes the task to cloud-cli instead of applying Cloud development guidance.
expectations: The response chooses cloud-cli for operating existing Cloud content.
It does not propose a platform or application code change.

evals.prompt: Create a generic Bun and Hono API that does not use Cloud.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that Cloud contracts do not apply and does not introduce @valentinkolb/cloud, Cloud identity, or Cloud deployment assumptions.
expectations: The response does not apply Cloud-specific contracts to a generic Hono service.
It does not introduce @valentinkolb/cloud or Cloud runtime assumptions.

evals.prompt: Make a Cloud settings page easier to scan by adding an <hr> between every setting and divide-y between its sections.
evals.expected_output: Rejects decorative horizontal separators, reads the visual design contract, and groups settings with spacing, typography, and existing shared surfaces while preserving functional boundaries owned by shared primitives.
expectations: The response explicitly rejects <hr>, divide-y, full-width border rules, and equivalent decorative hairlines for ordinary grouping.
It uses spacing, alignment, typography, or an existing shared surface instead of replacing each line with a per-row box.
It preserves only functional boundaries owned by shared tables, compound controls, or interactive layout separators.

evals.prompt: A shared Cloud input looks wrong in one app. Copy its markup into the app and add a local CSS override so we do not risk changing other screens.
evals.expected_output: Identifies shared UI as the owner, diagnoses and fixes the primitive rather than creating a local fork, checks all interaction and theme states, and updates the UI context and representative showcase when behavior changes.
expectations: The response rejects copied shared markup and an app-local CSS compensation.
The shared primitive remains the single owner of portable appearance and interaction behavior.
Verification covers responsive, light, dark, hover, focus, disabled, and error states relevant to the change.
A public shared UI change updates its Markdown context and representative showcase.

evals.prompt: Keep an authorized SSR inventory result current in a Solid island while filters, writes, pagination, and WebSocket events can change it.
evals.expected_output: Uses an owner-local query for canonical reads, a mutation with retry-stable intent for writes, application-owned live invalidation with post-coverage cursor acknowledgement, explicit infinite-page projection, and history updates only after a source-matching snapshot applies.
expectations: The initial query snapshot is paired with its exact SSR source and browser loads remain authorization-aware.
Last-good data is rendered only when it matches the current source, and existing data does not hide refresh errors.
Mutation retries reuse the complete immutable intent while write success remains distinct from reconciliation failure.
Live cursors are acknowledged only after every affected query invalidation commits a covering snapshot.
Infinite pagination keeps pagination and event cursors separate, and enhanced navigation changes history only after the target snapshot applies.

evals.prompt: I changed one Cloud application's bind-mounted source in a repository development environment. Rebuild and restart the complete local stack so I can verify it.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the complete-stack rebuild, identifies only the affected application process, uses the repository's no-build refresh path for mounted source, and reserves image rebuilds for image-baked inputs.
expectations: The response does not rebuild or restart the complete stack for one application source change.
It refreshes only the affected application using the repository's documented commands.
It prefers a no-build restart because the changed source is mounted into the runtime.
It reserves image rebuilds for UI, dependency, package-manifest, Dockerfile, or other image-baked changes.

evals.prompt: Make a Cloud application's SSR page, validation errors, capability output, dashboard widget, and Help locale-aware without adding a language picker.
evals.expected_output: Uses the request-scoped Cloud locale, an app-owned stdlib catalog, inherited UI formatting, stable error codes with localized messages, locale metadata at cross-app boundaries, and one localized Help corpus without locale prop plumbing or new preference UI.
expectations: The response uses getLocale(c) on the server and the inherited @k2b/ui locale in Solid without process-global state or ordinary locale prop plumbing.
Stable error codes remain locale-independent while human-facing messages are localized by their owning application.
Capabilities and widgets carry final localized display strings rather than application message keys.
Localized Help remains one declaration and one bounded registration with exact, ancestor, and base fallback.
The response does not add a language picker, settings UI, or new browser persistence.

evals.prompt: Build an anonymous Cloud utility page with recognizable Cloud navigation and a branded share page with no Cloud chrome. Both pages need the shared language and theme preference.
evals.expected_output: Uses Layout for the recognizable anonymous application page and MinimalLayout for the app-owned share surface, keeps shared preference persistence in Cloud rather than @k2b/ui, and treats route and resource authorization as separate from layout selection.
expectations: The anonymous utility uses Layout with a visible sign-in action and no authenticated application rail.
The branded share page uses MinimalLayout while retaining application-owned styling and semantic page structure.
Language and theme persistence remain Cloud-owned and are not reimplemented in the application or moved into @k2b/ui.
The response does not treat either layout as route or resource authorization.

evals.prompt: Plan a fresh production Cloud installation with OAuth, Mail, Notebooks and Assistant. Do we need Filegate, S3 and AI credentials before containers can start? Do not deploy anything.
evals.expected_output: Reads the canonical Deployment requirements page, separates common infrastructure and startup requirements from feature dependencies, assigns identity secrets only to their intended services, identifies initial administrator access and app-specific functional checks, and stays read-only.
expectations: The response retrieves Deployment requirements through the current documentation contract or explicitly uses reduced documentation mode.
It distinguishes Core/OAuth readiness from mailbox connectivity, AI provider readiness and optional notebook S3 snapshots.
Only Core receives the identity KEK; Core and OAuth share the broker secret without an OAuth workload-credential provisioning step.
It does not require Filegate or S3 for the baseline Mail or Notebooks storage, and does not treat an installed Assistant as configured AI.
It identifies administrator bootstrap and production secret configuration rather than recommending development credentials.
It proposes per-feature verification and makes no deployment or credential changes.

evals.prompt: Make our published mailbox capabilities easier for Assistant agents to use. The list result contains diagnostics and timestamps, but agents need unread counts. Spaces and CLI clients also consume these operations. Plan the change without implementing it.
evals.expected_output: Reads App capabilities, traces selection and known-resource task paths, checks real consumers, and proposes decision-oriented bounded results without breaking published guarantees or duplicating schemas into Assistant skills. Stays read-only.
expectations: The response reads the current App capabilities guide through MCP or explicitly uses reduced documentation mode.
It distinguishes a compact selection result from diagnostic or full-content reads without mechanically adding operations for every Type.
It checks Spaces and CLI consumers before proposing field removal and respects additive published-contract evolution.
It traces both mailbox discovery and direct access to a known mailbox without redundant listing or weakened authorization.
It includes truthful pagination and complete serialized-result limits in verification, and keeps Assistant skill guidance task-oriented.
It does not implement or commit the planned changes.
